items.title: Uptake and retention in this service are unknown
items.whyItMatters: A definitive trial is only possible if enough young people take up peer support and stay in contact (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Measure uptake among eligible young people and retention at six months against pre-set criteria.

items.title: Peer workers leave when roles are unclear
items.whyItMatters: Turnover of 40 percent within a year (claim c3) would end the study early.
items.opportunity: Written role description, lived-experience supervision, and a measure of peer worker wellbeing.

items.title: Questionnaires are least complete for under-18s
items.whyItMatters: Missing outcomes in the youngest group bias any later trial.
items.opportunity: Use the shortest questionnaire, asked in person by a named worker.

items.title: Groups at highest risk of disengaging
items.whyItMatters: Young men, cannabis users and people without stable housing disengage most (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Report uptake and retention for these groups.

errorsFound: The first scan reply was prose rather than JSON and offered ratings without an appraisal; it was not applied.
reevaluation: The feasibility study should measure uptake, retention, delivery, peer worker wellbeing and questionnaire completion against progression criteria, with interviews to explain the numbers.
summary: Four gaps; uptake and retention, and peer worker turnover, are high severity.
